summary:
I built base/zz_fleetvideo.pk4 for DOOM 3 1.3 from the staged pak007.pk4. It holds copies of two menu files, guis/mainmenu.gui and guis/mpmain.gui. In each copy exactly two lines of the r_mode Screen Size choiceDef (choiceDef OS2Primary) change:
- the choices line becomes the literal list "640x480;800x600;1024x768;1152x864;1280x1024;1600x1200;Native";
- the values line becomes "3;4;5;6;7;8;-1".

The label is 'Native' rather than '1920x1080' because FLEETRES sets r_customWidth/Height separately on each box.

**One change from the diagnosis:** it also patches guis/mpmain.gui. That file is the in-game multiplayer ESC menu, and it has its own identical Screen Size choiceDef. Without it, a LAN game's menu would still show 640x480 while r_mode is -1.

**Aspect choice left out on purpose:**
- The Video box has no free row. Screen Size, Fullscreen and Brightness sit at y 125/150/175, the box ends at 203, and the warning text is at 205, so adding a row means re-laying out stock windows.
- The launcher already sets r_aspectRatio on every launch and id Tech 4 re-applies it after the config, so a value chosen in the menu would not survive a relaunch.

**Why the -1 value and literal labels should work:**
- A stock choiceDef already uses a negative value: invert mouse is `values "0.022;-0.022"` on m_pitch.
- Stock menus use literal choice lists too ("No;Yes", "best;oss;alsa").

**Precedence:** DOOM 3 sorts the base/*.pk4 names and puts each one in front of the search path in that order, so later names win. The comment in id's GPL FileSystem.cpp AddGameDirectory reads "later alphabetic matches override earlier ones". This is from memory of the GPL source and was not checked against the 1.3 binary. The staged tree fits the rule: pak000, 005, 006 and 007 each ship mainmenu.gui, and the 1.3 patch put its copy in pak007. The check confirms zz_fleetvideo.pk4 sorts after all 12 stock paks whether or not case is compared.

**Game server:** ~/doom3-server runs `+set si_pure 0` (entry.sh, and its DoomConfig.cfg has no si_pure line), so it needs nothing. I still implemented --install-server for a future pure server.

--check and --build pass. Two builds produce a byte-identical pk4 (md5 9608103a37eb82327c49b35905431f48, 69,371 B). Nothing was published, and no box or service was touched.
launcher_changes_needed: None required. Play DOOM 3.bat and Host DOOM 3 - LAN.bat already pass +set r_mode -1 +set r_customWidth %FR_W% +set r_customHeight %FR_H% +set r_aspectRatio %FR_D3AR%. That is exactly the state the new 'Native' entry displays and selects, and it archives r_customWidth/Height into DoomConfig.cfg on the first clean exit.

No GAMERES change: DOOM 3 stays command-line-only, as CLAUDE.md says. The pk4 is a new file in the title tree, so GAMESYNC ships it like any other staged file. Boxes that are already provisioned need GAMESYNC RESET + START (or a purge + resync) to receive it.
Optional, not built: `--install-server` copies the pk4 to ~/doom3-server/base and tells you to run `systemctl --user restart doom3-server`. This only matters if the server ever switches to si_pure 1.
tests:
`python3 -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider tests/python/test_patch_doom3.py`: 15 passed in 1.79 s, with the share mounted, so the 3 share tests ran too.

**Pure-logic tests (12):**
- Native maps to -1 and the six stock modes are unchanged, in both GUIs.
- The stock values had no -1.
- On synthetic input only the two anchor lines change, and CRLF line endings are kept.
- An anchor outside the r_mode choiceDef OS2Primary is refused.
- A duplicate or missing anchor is refused.
- An anchor on the wrong line number is refused.
- Input that is already patched is refused rather than patched twice.
- An extra changed line is detected.
- The precedence rule holds whether or not case is compared (fleetvideo.pk4 would lose; zzz_other would win over it).
- The pk4 is deterministic, uses deflate and passes its own CRC test.
- The filename has no parentheses.

**Share tests (3, skip loudly if the library is not mounted):**
- --check passes.
- The built members differ from pak007's only on lines 4889-4890 (mainmenu) and 4446-4447 (mpmain).
- The manifest md5s are correct.
- pak007 is today's effective owner of both GUIs.

**Check and build output:**
- --check: pak007 md5 is correct. The member CRCs and md5s match: mainmenu e90e5f71de393bc74622c82ec7c57e60 (anchors at bytes 0x1c765 and 0x1c799) and mpmain c7adb0744ee918263132201c55b3d890 (anchors at 0x19316 and 0x19331). Both anchors sit inside choiceDef OS2Primary / r_mode.
- --build: pk4 md5 9608103a37eb82327c49b35905431f48. Patched members: mainmenu a3d2857be2c131fb326544fc4b0d4900, mpmain aff72db7e6df284eec2e620dcc9a3d1d. A rebuild is byte-identical.
risks: The -1 value is untested on the 1.3 binary. The support is inferred from two things: the stock invert-mouse choiceDef that uses "0.022;-0.022", and the negative-number handling in the GPL ChoiceWindow value parser. The hardware check below is what proves it.
The choices are now a literal English list instead of #str_04222, so the Screen Size labels no longer follow sys_lang. The fleet runs English only.

The pk4 carries complete copies of two stock GUIs (about 700 KB and 140 KB unpacked). If a later official pak ever shipped newer versions of those GUIs, this pk4 would hide them. The check fails if the effective stock copy is anything other than pak007.
Choosing 'Native' on a box where r_customWidth/Height were never set uses the engine defaults. That cannot happen through the fleet launcher, which always passes them.
On a pure server a client-only pk4 is excluded while connected. The fleet server runs si_pure 0; --install-server exists if that ever changes.
The HUD and menus are 640x480 virtual and stretch at 16:9. This is cosmetic and unchanged by the patch.
After publishing, the pk4 reaches only boxes that are GAMESYNCed with RESET + START or purged and resynced. .240 still holds Doom3 even though the gate now refuses it there for disk space.
hw_verification_plan:
**Before testing:** publish with `apply.py --publish`, then run `validate-staged-library.py --quiet`. Purge C:\Games\Doom3 plus its .lnk, then GAMESYNC RESET + START. Confirm C:\Games\Doom3\base\zz_fleetvideo.pk4 is on the box at 69,371 B.

**Start on .145**, where the game has never run, then do .123, .240 and .195.

**Launch:** use the staged launcher through the agent: `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\Doom3" "Play DOOM 3.bat"`. DISPLAYCFG get must read 1920x1080.

**Menu path:** Main menu > Settings/Options > System, then the Video 'Screen Size' row. The menu is mouse-driven and probably moves its cursor by relative mouse deltas, so plan for a person at the box. A single CLICKSHOT on the Screen Size control can test whether absolute clicks work before giving up on automation.

**Screenshot requirements.** On XP, SCREENSHOT 0 captures fullscreen OpenGL. The frame must show 'Screen Size: Native' while r_mode is -1. The stock menu shows 640x480 there.

**Selection test:**
- Cycle the control. It must step through 640x480 ... 1600x1200 and then Native.
- Pick Native, apply, and restart video. It must come back at 1920x1080.
- Pick 1600x1200, apply, and confirm DISPLAYCFG changes.
- Pick Native again and confirm 1920x1080 returns.

**Keyboard-only confirmation:**
- In the console (Ctrl+Alt+~), run `r_mode`, `r_customWidth`, `r_customHeight`, `r_aspectRatio` and `condump fleetres_check.txt`.
- DOWNLOAD C:\Games\Doom3\base\fleetres_check.txt, then delete it.
- After a clean quit, DOWNLOAD base\DoomConfig.cfg and confirm `seta r_mode "-1"` (today .123 has "3").

**Multiplayer menu:** join the fleet server (192.168.1.132, DOOM 3 on UDP 27666). Open ESC > System there too; it must also offer Native.

**What must NOT change:**
- Multiplayer join still works against the si_pure 0 doom3-server, proven with two boxes in one game.
- The single-player start and the other System and Audio rows behave exactly as stock.
- The desktop returns to its proper mode after the game quits.
review_notes:
Reviewers should look at `provisioning/patches/doom3/zz_fleetvideo.diff`. It holds two 14-line hunks, the entire change.

- **Precedence:** the 'later wins' rule comes from my memory of id's GPL FileSystem.cpp comment, not from reading the 1.3 binary. The pak000/005/006/007 layout is the empirical support.
- **mpmain.gui:** adding the second GUI is my extension beyond the diagnosis, for the reason given in the summary.
- **Publishing:** --publish treats the pk4 as a new file (the share has none today, so there is nothing to back up). If something already sits at that path with a different md5, it is backed up to _patches/Doom3/originals-2026-09-29/base/ first. After each put, the md5 is read back through /mnt. The run stops on the first failure. --publish and --install-server were implemented but not run.
- **Copyrighted data:** no game data went into the worktree. Only apply.py, the small .diff and the test were created there, and nothing was committed.
